title: Flex Headroom Pods — pricing experiment and enterprise SQ runbook
creator: Ava Kim
description: Overview: Run a staged pricing and contract experiment for a new Dedicated offering called 'Flex Headroom Pods' — a reserved GPU unit that includes configurable headroom (burst minutes) and soft autoscale credits. Objective: find a pricing construct that increases attach rate for mid-market customers (100k-1M ARR) while preserving uplift for enterprise deals and limiting revenue leakage from burst-heavy workloads. Hypothesis: bundling predictable reserved baseline plus small, priced headroom pods will increase conversion from trial to reserved, reduce overage disputes, and provide upsell motion to larger reserved bands. Key metrics: attach rate, monthly recurring revenue (MRR) from reserved seats, burst overage revenue, churn due to throttling, sales cycle length change, and NRR impact. Experiment variants: (A) Baseline: current reserved SKU + per-minute burst overage; (B) Flex-1: reserved baseline + 500 headroom minutes/month included; (C) Flex-2: reserved baseline + 2,000 headroom minutes/month + discounted overage; (D) Flex OnRamp: small monthly reserved + auto-convert to larger reserved after 90 days of sustained usage. For each variant we will simulate billing on historical usage buckets, run price elasticity modelling, and run a small customer pilot (n=8 customers, mix of AI-native startups & ISVs). Deliverables: pricing page copy, updated contract clause (SQ questions: encryption/KMS, SLA fallback, data residency), pilot scorecard, billing implementation spec, and experiment retrospective. Stakeholders: PM (Ava Kim), Sales lead (Priya Shah), Finance (Liam O'Connor), Legal (Marina Lopez), Engineering leads (runtime: Suresh Rao, billing: Mei Chen), Solutions Eng (Noah Patel).

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers consuming headroom rather than converting to larger reserved can reduce revenue yield. Mitigation: keep included minutes conservative; add progressive discounts for conversion and alerting to users + SEs.
Risk: Billing disputes around proration and mid-cycle upgrades. Mitigation: strong invoice line-iteming and beta contract clause; test end-to-end in sandbox with 3 sample invoices.
Risk: Security/SQ blockers from enterprise customers. Mitigation: preflight SQ update and Security review before pilot; provide KMS integration timeline in playbook.
Risk: Increased load on autoscale pools due to unpredictable burst patterns. Mitigation: rate-limit fallback and cross-region failover policies; daily consumption caps for pilot accounts.

Instrument each pilot with billing tags and runtime metrics; validate telemetry within 48 hours
Run pilot for 6 weeks with weekly checkpoints; collect usage, sales feedback, and billing disputes
Apply learnings to iterate on pricing bands and contract language; present retrospective and recommendation to GTM and Finance
